$comment: Written at merge time from the pilot run. data/distill/llm-finglish.jsonl.br is GENERATED by training/tiny_finglish_training/build_distill.py --merge.

source.words: 4-18 per sentence, Persian letters only; the chat round 2-12 (HomoRich) and 1+ (chat lines)
source.leakageGuard: load_gold_keys(*EVALUATION_FILES) on leak_key (the sentence's folded words, not the raw string): gold, quarantined gold, dev, the fixtures and both chat sets excluded before sampling; the chat round also drops a line sharing four words running with a chat-dev or chat-test message (load_ngrams)
source.$comment: Three samples over the same pool. Seed 20260915 drew the first 3,000; seed 20260916 drew 7,050 more; seed 20260917 drew 3,000 more, this time NOT uniformly. Each round excluded the ids already in the artifact before anything was typed (--exclude-typed), so no sentence is sampled twice. The pool was 413,734 sentences and 403,685 after removing the first two rounds.
source.targeting: Round 3 (shards 69-89) is a targeted draw: all 3,000 sentences end in a word written with a final ه (build_distill.ends_in_he), because the corpus under-represented that position by three to six times. HomoRich is written Persian and spells the copula است, where people type it as a ه on the word before: 3.4% of the eligible pool ends in a ه word against 9.7% of the dev set's human typing and 18.9% of the gold set's. The merged corpus is 16.6% of sentences ending that way. The remaining 7,000 of the round (shards 90-137, a uniform draw over everything not already taken, 2.9% ه-final) are exported but NOT typed.
source.chatRound: Round 4 (shards 138-149, seed 20260926) is chat. Shards 138-142: 700 HomoRich sentences drawn with --targeted-predicate chat-word (a word from data/chat/chat-words.txt and none of its written-register markers), 2-12 words, from 6,782 eligible. Shards 143-149: 1,001 LLM-written chat lines (data/chat/chat-lines.jsonl, ids ch-), 18 of 1,019 dropped by the chat leakage guard. Shards 90-137 (the untyped uniform draw of round 3) are still untyped, which is why this round starts at 138.

workers.claude: Claude Opus 5 in-session subagents, shards 0-17 (5,400 variants)
workers.luna: Codex CLI 0.154.0, gpt-5.6-luna, reasoning xhigh, herdr panes. Shards 18-19 in the pilot (600 variants); shards 20-68 in the scale-up (14,144 variants), typed by 10 agents in parallel; shards 69-89 in the targeted round (5,737 variants kept), typed by 5 agents. Shards 67-68 are a repair pass from the scale-up. Every shard 69-89 was gated by check_typing.py before merge. Shards 138-149 in the chat round (3,366 variants kept of 3,402), typed by 5 agents on Codex CLI 0.157.x, gated by check_typing.py before merge.

prompt.workerRules: Every worker was told to type each word by hand and never to write code that produces Finglish; to read only the prompt, its own shard and its own output file; and to append every ~25 sentences with a quoted heredoc. The heredoc rule was added mid-run: Finglish apostrophes had been breaking shell-argument quoting and damaging 2.2% of lines.
prompt.habitEnforcement: luna's everyday persona missed two rates stated in the card (aa ~15/100w, ~11 detached affixes/100w). The worker prompt restated them; the card itself was not edited. Measured over the 7,049 new sentences, luna/everyday then sat at aa 21.8 and detached 14.1 against the human's 18.4 and 10.8 - habit L1 0.34, closer to the human than claude/everyday's 0.35. Round 3: restating the rates in the worker prompt failed three times - luna/everyday came back at aa 42, 33 and 36 per 100 words against a 13-27 band, with 36% of persona pairs byte-identical on the first attempt. Prose does not control the rate. What worked was giving the worker the measuring instrument: check_typing.py --partial --strict after every 25-sentence batch. Under that loop a worker measured 37.7, deleted its own batch and retyped it unprompted. Round 3 landed at everyday aa 26.0 / detached 9.1, careful aa 39.1 / detached 1.2, identical pairs 13.6%, with 0 of 21 files outside their band. The card was not edited.
prompt.yield: Round 3 lost 263 of ~6,000 variants to the merge validator, all length mismatches and 202 of them one string short. The targeted subset is colloquial and HomoRich writes colloquial compounds with a space - بی ادبا, کشته های, لذت بخشه - which typists read as one word and type as one string, against the prompt's one-string-per-Persian-word rule. Earlier rounds had 3 such refusals in ~20,000 variants. The validator drops them, so the cost is yield and not corpus quality: 2,922 of the 3,000 targeted sentences survived.
prompt.chatRound: Same prompt and personas, plus two notes in the worker message for this round only: loanwords may take their foreign spelling in both personas (مرسی as 'merci' about half the time, اوکی as 'ok'), the one place 'c' is allowed, because the ship rule needs `merci` on the model tier and the card otherwise forbids c; and short messages keep one string per Persian word. The typed round has merci 16, mersi 12. Identical persona pairs ran at 16-26% on the first finished shards, most of them containing a long ا, so careful was not really differing: workers were told to check each finished file and retype the careful line of identical pairs with an ا, which took the round to 9.4% (limit 15%). Round aggregate: everyday aa 20.8 / detached 8.5, careful aa 29.6 / detached 0.2, 0 of 12 files outside their band.

fidelityTest.method: scripts/fidelity.ts: LLM typists romanized the dev set faithful Persian; compared with the human typing of the same sentences
fidelityTest.humanEngineAccuracy: 68.4% (rules engine on human typing vs faithful, 299 rows)

v1.verdict: failed: every persona exaggerated one habit (aa 38/100w vs human 18; u 7 vs 0.3; final eh 13 vs 1)

v2.engineOnLlmTyping: 80.3% / 85.8% vs 67.0% human on the same rows
v2.verdict: passed on habits; still easier to convert than human typing

alignment.$comment: 4.9% at 3,000 sentences, 6.6% at 10,049. Rows now carry their sentence id, for mix --llm-split sentence.

devStrictFaithfulFixtures.$comment: Re-fit from the larger corpus and kept: it gains on all three rule-engine tiers. It costs the hybrid 0.3 strict (57.9 -> 57.6) and leaves the model untouched.

modelRetrain.config: 102k architecture unchanged (d_model 64, d_hidden 96, 2 layers), int6; 110,018 params after the label vocabulary grew

arms.$comment: dev strict / dev faithful / fixtures, model engine, all at 10,049 sentences unless noted

learningCurvePureLlm.$comment: Pure LLM data, dev strict, by sentences typed. The 750/1500/3000 points are the earlier claude-heavy corpus; 2512/5024/10049 are nested subsets of the merged one. The intermediate points are non-monotonic, so read about +-1 point of noise into any single step: each arm picks its checkpoint on its own mixed dev and the label vocabularies differ (103,713 / 103,973 / 104,688 params).
learningCurvePureLlm.verdict: Still paying. 3,000 -> 10,049 is +3.3 points over 1.74 doublings, about +1.9 per doubling, the same rate as before and above the +1 stop rule. The 50% mix gained only +0.6 over the same range because mix() upsamples the LLM half to the synthetic count: the train set is 857k either way, so more sentences buy diversity (repetition fell from ~8.6x to ~2.6x), not exposure.

modelRetrain.metric: dev strict / dev faithful / fixtures, model engine

gold.$comment: scored once, at the end, never during tuning
gold.zwnjFixtures: 56.3% placement, was 41%; gold's Persian side carries no ZWNJ so its ZWNJ tier is structurally 0

uses.generatorFix: training/tiny_finglish_training/g2p.py wrote Persian letters (ع ئ ء ؤ) into the Latin side of 21,008 of 425,590 synthetic examples; fixed before any arm was trained

termsOfUse: Outputs of Claude (Anthropic) and GPT-5.6 luna (OpenAI) are used to fit a 1 KiB channel table and to train a 110k-parameter transliterator. Recorded so a reader can check this against the providers current terms; a character-level transliterator is not a general model competing with either.
